answer_1.outputs: The model generates text for tasks such as open-domain QA, document classification, named entity recognition, relation extraction, natural language inference, and question answering, often producing full-sentence answers.

answer_2.quote: For QA and OpenQA, we observe standard conventions and evaluate the predicted free text with the Exact Match metric, as initiated by .

answer_4.quote: We hire three expert human annotators proficient in English and with biomedical competencies to manually scrutinize model predictions, randomly sampling 120 test set instances (30 from each BioASQ dataset and 30 from MedQA-USMLE).
answer_4.guideline: We ask the graders to (i) binary label the scientific accuracy (factual correctness) of the generated answers, (ii) assess language fluency on a 3-point Likert scale from 1 (worst) to 3 (best).
